name: Ellen
role: protagonist; woman who learns to stop waiting and begin living
appearance: Full-figured woman in her early fifties, Caucasian, medium build with kind, tired brown eyes and short wavy salt-and-pepper hair. Dresses modestly in modern, comfortable clothing—sweaters, a plain gray knit, and a saved dress with soft fabric folds. Often shown with a Bible and a cup of coffee.
script_spans: "I did everything right," she whispered to the empty room.
Ellen was forty-nine years old, and she liked to say she had waited well.
"For thirty years," she said, "I thought God forgot to choose me."

name: Sharon (sister-in-law)
role: sister-in-law; casual well-meaning critic whose remarks push Ellen to honesty and reconnection
appearance: Full-figured woman in her late forties to early fifties, African American, medium-tall, with smooth dark skin, shoulder-length straightened hair, and contemporary church attire—floral blouse or smart cardigan and slacks. Warm but habitually talkative expression; often holding a wine glass or seated at a family table.
script_spans: "You will come, of course," Sharon said. "It will be good for you. Weddings are hard when you are, well."
"No date tonight?" Sharon asked, holding her wine, tilting her head.
"I did not know it landed that hard," Sharon said at last, quiet, not quite meeting her eyes.
